correctness.rationale: Finite Ewens singleton count chain has +1 probability theta/(theta+j), -1 probability k/(theta+j), and stay otherwise. On logarithmic time, Gnedin–Stark 2022 Theorem 6 gives a stationary immigration-death process; initial j<eps*n contributes <=eps, ensuring joint weak occupation-fraction limits, and bounded fractions imply covariance limits. Stationary reversibility and thinning from X(0)=0 yield Poisson(theta(1-e^-t)) at lag t, hence E[W0 Wd] equals e^-2theta theta^d/d! integral_0^1 e^(theta u)(1-u)^d du. I_d(0)=1/(d+1), I_d strictly increasing to infinity, and I_(d+1)<I_d yield unique increasing thresholds; Gaussian upper/lower Laplace bounds at theta=d+(1+-eta)sqrt(d log d) prove sharp first-order displacement. Independent SciPy integration/bisection gave theta1=1.793282132900761, theta2=3.383634282853483, theta3=4.881277491345546.
residual_risks: n tends to infinity with fixed d and theta; large-d root limit is mathematically separate and no uniform n,d theorem is proved.

value.rationale: The empirical occupation fractions are natural observables for Ewens growth precisely because they fluctuate rather than converge almost surely. Their 0-versus-d covariance changing from negative to positive despite pointwise mutual exclusion is a motivated nontrivial phase phenomenon. A full ordered family of exact thresholds and the sqrt(d log d) displacement are specific reusable facts, not a routine finite sample or a restatement of the classical Poisson queue kernel.
residual_risks: Not a finite-n covariance sign result or uniform joint d,n limit; dependence beyond the selected two occupations is not classified.
